fact: Co-author Jean-Francois Henrotte said at the 20 April 2026 launch of the book's second edition that the DRC has adopted a Digital Code whose Book III treats data protection extensively, replacing the embryonic provisions of the 2020 telecommunications law; the article does not say whether it is in force.

TechAfrica News reports that the government introduced its personal data legal framework in 2023 through Ordinance-Law No. 23/010, the Digital Code, which sets out lawful processing, transparency, data minimisation and system security, and treats it as the framework within which DPOs ensure compliance; the report gives no date for the statement, so the published date of 2026-03-17 is used.

The report says the DPO network forms part of the national data governance effort 'aligned with ... plans to establish a dedicated Data Protection Authority', so the authority is planned and not yet established; no date is given for the statement, so the published date of 2026-03-17 is used.

The Ministry of Digital Economy launched a national Data Protection Officers (DPO) network in Kinshasa to build professional capacity and promote best practice in personal data protection, with Minister Augustin Kibassa Maliba presiding; no sanction or decision is reported; the report gives no event date, so the published date of 2026-03-17 is used.
The launch of the national DPO network in March 2026 is reported as a step in strengthening data governance ahead of a planned Data Protection Authority; the published date of 2026-03-17 is used.

We Are Tech Africa reports that the DPO network comes three years after adoption of ordonnance-loi n°23/010 on the Digital Code, which sets the principles of lawful, transparent and secure processing of personal data and under which DPOs operate; the report gives no separate date for the statement, so the published date of 2026-03-16 is used.

The Minister of Digital Economy says the DPO network precedes the 'création prochaine' of a national Data Protection Authority, so the authority is not yet created; the published date of 2026-03-16 is used.

On Thursday 12 March 2026 in Kinshasa the Ministry of Digital Economy launched the national network of data protection officers, to standardise personal data practice and support compliance in the public and private sectors, backed by RUDI International and Droit-Numérique.cd; no sanction or decision is reported.
The national DPO network was launched on 12 March 2026 ahead of the announced creation of the Data Protection Authority.

On 6 August 2024 the think tank Law & Technologies presented a study saying the Data Protection Authority required by Article 262 of the Digital Code (cited in the article as Loi 20/017) exists on paper but is not yet operational, and called on the government to draft and sign the decree fixing its organisation and functioning.

fact: Ordonnance-loi n° 23/010 of 13 March 2023 on the Digital Code was made by the President; its Book III sets the rules on public data and the protection of personal data (Article 166); the passages read contain no commencement provision, so only enactment is recorded.

Article 262 creates an independent administrative Autorité de protection des données with legal personality and administrative and financial autonomy, and says a Prime Minister's decree will fix its organisation and functioning; Articles 267 to 268 set the membership conditions and a four-member bureau; the document does not show it constituted.

The Droit-Numérique.cd analysis states that Ordonnance-loi n° 23/010 of 13 March 2023 on the Digital Code, which provides for the Autorité de Protection des Données, entered into force in 2023; the document gives no more exact date for entry into force, so the year is recorded.

The analysis states that Articles 262 to 270 of the Digital Code provide for the Autorité de Protection des Données, to be set up by Prime Ministerial decree, and that a ministerial order of 17 August 2024 (n° CAB/MIN/PT&N/AKIM/KL/KBS/051/2024) provisionally transferred its missions to ARPTIC pending its establishment; the document does not say ARPTIC has acted in that role.

ACTPOL says the DRC's Digital Code (Ordinance-Law No. 23/010 of 13 March 2023) created a Data Protection Authority that has not been set up, and a ministerial order of August 2024 gave its functions to the telecommunications regulator meanwhile.
